decision.note: RULE (b) chosen by Sam, 2026-08-21, on run C inc-126. Only the pages the overview links to end with the three controls; a page reached from another page ends with the primary alone. The party pickers stay as they are; seven second-and-later task-row pages lose their return controls (consignment details, import purpose, port of exit, exit date, transporter selection, private transporter details, CPH number). Mechanism: a fourth parameter showReturnControls on src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13, defaulting true, with the seven named templates and the party pickers passing false. KNOCK-ON: the hub-to-overview rename lands on 29 frontend screens rather than 41.

finding.frontend:
A trader filling in a notification meets one of six different endings to a page, and cannot predict which. On 41 of the 67 captured frontend screens the page ends with three controls — a primary button, a secondary "Save and return to hub" button and a "Cancel and return to hub" link. On the other 26 the page offers no way to save what has been entered and leave. The two return controls always travel together: on every screen where either appears the other does too, because one shared macro builds all three unconditionally and takes no argument that would drop one (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13).

What decides which pages get them is not anything a user can see. Nineteen feature templates call that macro, and they are exactly the nineteen answer pages of the linear flow other than the dashboard (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:31-86). Anything routed outside that flow ends the page its own way. So the split falls inside a single section of the service: the CPH number page and the five party pickers are both reached from rows on the consignment addresses page, and the CPH page offers all three controls while Place of origin offers only "Save and continue" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:109, its label duplicated in a copy key of its own at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:62). A trader who wants to stop halfway can do it on one and not on the other.

The primary beside them is not one button either but three labels out of four copy keys: "Save and continue" from the shared key on 30 screens (src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45), "Save and finish" on the four animal-identification states (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/animal-identification.njk:25), and "Continue" on the seven documents and consignment-addresses states (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:92 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/template.njk:16).

The 26 screens with no return control break down as nine party-picker states ending with a lone "Save and continue"; five check-your-answers and declaration states ending with a lone "Continue" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/template.njk:112 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/template.njk:42); the delete-notification and cancel-amendment confirmations, which pair a primary with a secondary link back; and ten overview, dashboard and confirmation states, which carry page-specific controls rather than the journey pattern and sit outside this finding. Giving a party picker the return controls is not a template edit alone: its post always redirects to the consignment addresses page and never reads the exit value the secondary button submits (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:92, against the shared helpers at src/server/app/shared/kit.js:77-89).
finding.prototype:
Design release 1 offers no rule to copy, because it does not follow one itself. Across its 60 captured screens the three-control ending appears on 29; the primary reads "Save and continue" on 45 screens and "Continue" on 7; and the cancel control has three destinations rather than one — "Cancel and return to overview" as a link on the 29, "Cancel and return to dashboard" as a secondary button on three, and "Cancel and return to address book" as a secondary button on three. Unlike the frontend, the two return controls do not travel together here: six screens offer a way to cancel and no way to save and return.

The inconsistency lands inside the design's own structures, so no reading of it produces a rule. Of the twelve pages the overview links to (app/routes.js:5749-5841), ten end with all three controls, but origin-of-the-import ends with a single "Save and continue" — inside the very same form-actions wrapper the three-control pages use, with the second button and the cancel paragraph simply absent (app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:167-175) — and contact-address-for-consignment ends with a bare "Continue" (app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:86). Below the consignment-parties row its three sibling sub-pages disagree with each other: permanent-address-animals carries all three (app/views/permanent-address-animals.html:104-120), cph-number carries one "Save and continue" (app/views/cph-number.html:55-58) and consignment-address-select carries one (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:167-170). In transport the type chooser ends with a bare "Continue" (app/views/transporter-add.html:86) while the two forms below it end with "Save and continue" beside a secondary "Cancel and return to dashboard" (app/views/transporter-add-private.html:46-51), a destination that appears nowhere else in the notification journey.

There is no shared partial behind any of this. Eleven root views hand-write the block, nine of them repeating the same wrapper classes verbatim and two writing their own — app/views/consignment-details.html:136-154 against app/views/permanent-address-animals.html:104-120 — and the only journey-form-actions partials in the codebase belong to later releases, which no root view includes, so DR1 never had one place to state the rule in.

The design's own routing says the single-button pages are omissions rather than decisions. Fifteen post handlers accept the hub action that the secondary button submits, covering nineteen of the design's post routes (app/routes.js:1315-1317), and the handler behind origin-of-the-import is one of them: send it that action and it saves and redirects to the overview (app/routes.js:9265-9268). The page renders no button that would send it.

One arrangement difference runs through all 29: Design release 1 puts the two buttons on a row and the cancel link in a paragraph beneath them, where the frontend puts all three on one line.
finding.difference:
Make the ending of a journey page the same everywhere, on one rule, and apply it from one place. This replaces the earlier reading of the same evidence, which proposed stripping the return controls from the five frontend pages Design release 1 happens to end with one button; that would have copied the design's own inconsistency into the frontend rather than removing it, and it was dropped for that reason. Nothing here changes what any control says.

Deciding the rule needs a service owner, and that is why this is banded disputed: Design release 1 is signed off but does not state one, and neither of the two candidate rules can be read off it. The two are:

(a) Every page that collects an answer ends with the same three controls. Under this the frontend is nineteen-twentieths of the way there and the work is to bring the five party pickers into line: call the shared macro from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:109 instead of a bare button, and route the exit value through kit.exitTarget in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:92 so the secondary button has somewhere to go. The per-picker copy key at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:62 becomes dead and goes.

(b) Only the pages the overview links to end with the three controls, and a page reached from another page ends with the primary alone. Under this the party pickers stay as they are and seven pages lose their return controls — the second-and-later pages of the task rows at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:27-59, namely consignment details, import purpose, port of exit, exit date, transporter selection, private transporter details and CPH number.

The mechanism is the same either way and belongs in the shared macro, not in copies of a shortened button group. Give src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13 a fourth parameter, showReturnControls, defaulting to true, and wrap the secondary button and the cancel link in it. Under (a) no template passes it and the party pickers adopt the macro; under (b) the seven templates named above pass false — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/template.njk:25, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.njk:31, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-purpose/template.njk:24, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/template.njk:23, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/template.njk:15, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.njk:25 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/private-transporter-details/private-transporter-details.njk:92 — and the party pickers adopt the macro passing false, so that every ending in the service comes out of one file. Whichever rule is chosen, the review section and the two confirmation pages keep the endings they have: check your answers and the declaration read "Continue" alone on both sides already, and delete and cancel-amendment are confirm-or-go-back pages that Design release 1 does not have.

What would settle the choice is a ruling on one sentence: may a trader stop and save from every page that asks a question, or only from the pages the overview sends them to. Design release 1 answers it both ways on adjacent pages of the same section, so the answer has to come from the service owner rather than from the design.

Two boundaries with neighbouring findings, both of which change what these controls say and neither of which changes where they appear. service-wide--primary-button-says-continue-not-save-and-continue owns the text of the primary button. service-wide--save-and-cancel-buttons-name-the-hub owns the text of the two return controls. This finding changes no string at all; it changes which pages render the controls, and it is the only one of the three that needs a decision before it can start. Order does not matter between them: the renames touch copy keys and this touches the macro's parameters and its callers. One knock-on worth flagging to whoever picks up the renames: if rule (b) is chosen, the two return controls end up on seven fewer pages than they are on today — twelve fewer captured screens, because four of those seven pages were photographed in more than one state — so the rename lands on 29 frontend screens rather than 41.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a shared partial or macro in Design release 1's root views that renders the end-of-page controls — one file every root journey view includes — which would mean the design does state a single rule and the work is to follow it rather than to choose one.
finding.verification:
Verified by a different agent than wrote it, against the two pinned checkouts (git rev-parse confirms the frontend at 76a864ba93ac7c60d358c902bd68396731daacf3 and the prototype at 491b39263e4f3b613bc398851b701425b74438ee) and against all 67 frontend and 60 Design release 1 files under capture/html/. The central claim survives. Six numbers or sentences were wrong and are corrected in the slots; each is named below.

Counts re-derived here rather than taken from the author. "Save and return to hub" and "Cancel and return to hub" each match 41 of the 67 frontend captures, and sorting the two file lists and diffing them returns nothing, so the two controls never appear apart — that is the whole of the travel-together claim, checked rather than asserted. The 26 remainder, listed with grep -L, are the nine party-picker states, three check-answers states, two declaration states, fe-delete-notification, fe-cancel-amend, seven dashboard states, two hub states and fe-confirmation: the author's 9 / 5 / 2 / 10 breakdown exactly. On the requirements side "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" each match 29 of the 60 captures and the same files; "Cancel and return to dashboard" matches three and "Cancel and return to address book" three, and diffing every file carrying "Save and return to" against every file carrying "Cancel and return to" leaves exactly those six, so three destinations and six cancel-without-save both hold. Primary labels on that side: 45 files carry "Save and continue" and seven carry a bare "Continue" (declaration and its error state, review-notification and its incomplete state, transporter-add, contact-address-for-consignment, address-book-add).

The strongest claim — the 19-to-19 correspondence — is exact. Grepping src/server for saveActions returns 19 invocation sites in 19 feature templates. Listing the pages of src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:31-86 by hand gives 23: dashboardPage, the three review pages (notificationViewPage, declarationPage, confirmationPage) and 19 others. I matched those 19 one-for-one onto the 19 templates with nothing left over on either side. The party-picker template is the twentieth answer-collecting template and it is the one that does not call the macro, which is what "nineteen-twentieths" means and it is fair.

The decisive claim survives at source, and I attacked it three ways. app/routes.js:1315-1317 is isJourneySoftSaveAction, true for 'hub' and for 'review'. Grep returns 16 call sites besides the definition; reading the enclosing handler for each gives 15 post handlers, because reason-for-import tests it twice (:10216 and :10268), and one of the 15 is handleConsignmentAddressSelectPost at :3838, registered on all five selectable consignment-address sections at :10914-10919, so 19 post routes accept it. The author wrote "sixteen post handlers"; the slot now reads fifteen handlers over nineteen routes. The origin half is sound: router.post('/origin-of-the-import') writes countryOfOrigin, regionOfOriginRequired and internalReference into the session at :9242-9244 before reaching :9265-9268, so action=hub does save and then redirect to /notification-hub, skipping validation to do it. app/views/origin-of-the-import.html renders exactly one govukButton, at :169-173, inside the same app-origin-form-actions wrapper the three-control pages use; grepping that whole file for 'action' returns only the macro import, the form's own action attribute and that one button. Nothing on the page can send it.

The partial claim, which the whole finding rests on, holds. find over app/ for *form-actions* returns only app/views/partials/design-release-2/journey-form-actions.html and app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html; grepping every view outside those two release subfolders for journey-form-actions returns nothing at all, so no root view includes either; and neither app/views/layouts/main.html nor app/views/layouts/journey.html contains a govukButton, a form-actions wrapper or a cancel link. app/views/ holds exactly 30 root .html files and exactly 11 contain "Save and return to overview", so 11 of 30 is right. But "each with its own wrapper markup" was wrong: nine of the eleven repeat app-origin-form-actions, app-origin-actions and app-origin-form-actions__cancel verbatim, and only permanent-address-animals and transporter write their own names — the pair the author chose as the example happens to be one of the two that differ. Corrected; it does not weaken the finding, because eleven hand-written copies remain eleven places to edit.

Read app/routes.js:5749-5841 line by line: twelve overview items across six sections, counting both conditional ones. Intersected against the eleven three-control views: ten match, and the two that do not are origin-of-the-import and contact-address-for-consignment, as claimed. permanent-address-animals is the eleventh three-control view and the overview does not link to it, which the finding implies and does not overstate. The three consignment-parties siblings check out at source — app/views/permanent-address-animals.html:104-122 all three, app/views/cph-number.html:55-58 one, app/views/consignment-address-select.html:166-169 one — with one qualification left in the record rather than in the prose: a secondary "Add a new address" govukButton sits immediately above that last primary at :160-164, so "carries one" there means one control in the save-and-return sense, not one button on the page.

Both corrections to the dropped inc-106 hold. dr1-transporter-add-private.html:581 and dr1-transporter-add-commercial.html:490 each render "Cancel and return to dashboard" as a submit button carrying name=action and value=cancel with govuk-button--secondary — a button, not the link inc-106 called it — and inc-106's prose names only the private page, so it did miss the commercial one. Source agrees at app/views/transporter-add-private.html:44-56.

The "four primaries" claim was wrong and is corrected to three. Within the 41 the labels are "Save and continue" on 30 (39 frontend files carry the string, nine of them party pickers outside the 41), "Save and finish" on the four animal-identification states, and "Continue" on the four documents and three addresses-hub states: 30 + 4 + 7 = 41. Four copy keys produce those three labels, because two separate per-feature keys are both set to "Continue" — .../features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:8 and .../features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:51 — which is the likeliest source of the author's four. The slot now reads three labels out of four copy keys.

The stated knock-on was wrong and is corrected. Rule (b)'s seven pages I re-derived by listing every row of task-rows.js:27-59 and taking the second and later pages: consignmentDetails, importPurpose, portOfExit, exitDate, transportersSelect, privateTransporterDetails, cphNumber — the author's list exactly. But those seven pages are twelve captured screens. I read the url of each from capture/model/frontend/: three consignment-details states, two port-of-exit, two cph-number, two transporter-private, and one each of import-purpose, exit-date and transporter-commercial — the last of which resolves to /transporters/select, so it is transportersSelect and fe-transporter-type is the transporter row's first page and keeps its controls under (b). 41 minus 12 is 29, not 34, and the difference slot now says 29 with the page-versus-screen distinction spelled out. This matters to whoever picks up inc-105, which is why the finding flags it.

One user-facing sentence was untrue. "On the other 26 there is no way out of the page except forward" is contradicted by the captures: every one of those pages renders breadcrumbs and a back link (capture/html/frontend/fe-address-picker-place-of-origin.html:93-102 shows both), and the paragraph four sentences later already said delete-notification and cancel-amend end with a secondary "No, return to..." control. What is absent is a way to save and leave, so the slot now says that. I checked the party pickers' and check-answers' endings in the captured DOM directly: fe-address-picker-place-of-origin ends with a lone "Save and continue" at :361-363 (its only other button is the mid-page "Search"), fe-check-answers at :520-522 and fe-declaration at :153-155 with a lone "Continue".

Citations. Every frontend path in the file is full and repo-relative from src/; every prototype path is a root view under app/views/, and grepping the file for design-release-2, design-release-2.1 and testing returns zero, so the highest-yield trap in this corpus is not sprung. Two frontend citations were a line out, pointing at the closing form tag rather than the button, and are fixed to check-answers/template.njk:112 and declaration/template.njk:42. Confirmed at source, line by line: save-actions.njk:3-13 (three controls, one button-group, no parameter that could drop one), shared/copy.en.js:42-45, kit.js:77-89 (hubExitTarget at :77, exitTarget at :85), _address-picker.njk:109, addresses/copy/copy.en.js:62, party-picker.controller.js:92 (redirects to the addresses page; grepping that file for 'exit' returns nothing, so it genuinely cannot honour the secondary button), flow.js:31-86, task-rows.js:27-59, and all seven rule-(b) template lines. Four prototype ranges stop a line or two short of the block they name (consignment-details runs :136-155, permanent-address-animals :104-122, transporter-add-private :44-56, consignment-address-select's primary opens at :166); each opens inside the right block and resolves, so they are left as written.

Band. disputed is declared for dr1c in tools/parity/corpora.json:850-855 and is used in the sense the contract admits: Design release 1 contradicts itself between its own screens — three siblings under consignment parties disagreeing with each other, and origin-of-the-import disagreeing with the ten other pages the overview links to — not "we do not want this". finding.difference names the one sentence that settles it, and nothing in the file hedges, asks permission or questions whether the design is authoritative.

Boundaries. Read inc-104 and inc-105 in workareas/journey-builder/EUDPA-328-DR1C/backlog.json: inc-104 owns the primary button's text, inc-105 owns the two return-control strings, and this finding proposes no string change anywhere — I searched its prose for a rename and found none. Both relatedTo ids resolve to files in findings/. No claim here rests on a volatile value; every label checked is a literal in source on both sides.

Verdict: corrected.

relatedTo.why: Both are about the same block at the foot of a journey page: that finding is what the primary button says, this one is whether the two return controls beside it are there at all.
That finding renames the save and cancel controls; this one decides which pages render them, so the rename's blast radius depends on which rule is chosen here.
